options.D: Take the diaphragm out, wash it, and reinsert it with fresh spermicide

explanation: For repeat intercourse, she should just push more spermicide straight into the vagina without taking the device out. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h5)

question: What term describes the condition where semen flows backward into the urinary bladder during climax?

options.A: Erectile failure
options.B: Azoospermia
options.C: Hypospadias
options.D: Retrograde ejaculation

explanation: Retrograde ejaculation happens when the bladder neck fails to close properly, forcing semen backward instead of forward. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h4)

question: Why must a community health nurse look at factors like poverty and local food markets?

options.A: To diagnose rare metabolic diseases in individuals
options.B: To manage hospital kitchen budgets
options.C: To calculate precise intravenous nutrition doses
options.D: These environmental factors directly impact what families can eat

explanation: Social and economic factors shape the food environment, which heavily dictates the nutritional habits of the community. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h1)

question: A nurse notices a patient's blood pressure dropping rapidly and calls the doctor using SBAR. What information should be stated in the Recommendation part?

options.A: What action or intervention is needed right now
options.B: A summary of yesterday's nursing shift notes
options.C: The patient's full medical history from childhood
options.D: The exact cost of the patient's hospital room

explanation: Correct! The 'Recommendation' is where you clearly state what you need done right now to help stabilize your patient. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h5)

question: What does healthcare interoperability allow different computer systems to do?

options.A: Communicate and exchange patient data accurately
options.B: Convert voice recordings into hand-written notes
options.C: Block all external internet traffic for safety
options.D: Automatically print paper prescriptions for patients

explanation: Think of interoperability like a bridge: it simply means different software and hospital gadgets can successfully talk and share information with each other. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h3)

question: When is a doctor most likely to prescribe a drug like ranolazine?

options.A: When the patient has an extremely slow resting heart rate
options.B: When standard drugs fail to control chronic stable angina
options.C: When treating an acute emergency heart attack in the ER
options.D: When high blood pressure is the primary diagnosis to treat

explanation: Think of ranolazine as a trusty backup plan—it's usually brought in when the usual first-line medications aren't quite getting the job done on their own. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h5)

question: What happens if money meant for the DRF is used to pay for unrelated hospital bills?

options.A: The prices of medicines in the hospital automatically decrease for all patients
options.B: The pharmacy runs out of stock because money is missing to buy new drugs
options.C: The pharmacy staff must pay for the missing inventory out of their own salaries
options.D: The government automatically replaces the missing funds within twenty-four hours

explanation: Because the DRF relies completely on its own cash flow, taking cash out for other projects breaks the cycle and leaves the shelves empty. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h1)

question: In healthcare finance, what does 'opportunity cost' mean?

options.A: The value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made
options.B: The total cost of operating a hospital for one calendar year
options.C: The penalty fee charged for mismanaged nursing budgets
options.D: The financial profit made from treating emergency patients

explanation: Opportunity cost is simply what you have to give up when you choose option A over option B. Every choice has a trade-off! [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h6)

question: A ward manager notices more patient falls happening. What should they do right after gathering this data?

options.A: Write a brand new job description for the ward clerk
options.B: Ignore the data until the end of the fiscal year audit
options.C: Compare the fall rates against the established hospital safety benchmark
options.D: Immediately fire the nurses working the night shift without investigation

explanation: Once you collect the data, the logical next step is to compare it to your hospital's safety standard to see how big the gap is. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h2)

question: Why did 19th-century visiting nurses check on housing conditions as well as treating patients?

options.A: Hospital administrators required them to inspect neighborhood buildings
options.B: Patients refused medical treatment unless their landlords fixed the plumbing
options.C: Environmental factors directly drove the spread of urban infectious diseases
options.D: Government policies banned nurses from giving medicine without housing checks

explanation: Nurses quickly realized that treating an illness is a waste of time if the patient just goes back to a dirty, overcrowded room that made them sick in the first place! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why do some oral medications need to be given in much higher doses than IV (intravenous) medications?

options.A: To ensure the drug binds tightly to red blood cells instantly
options.B: To prevent the stomach acid from expanding the capsule size
options.C: To make up for drug lost to the first-pass effect in the liver
options.D: To speed up the rate of renal filtration in the kidneys

explanation: When you swallow a pill, the liver catches and breaks down a good chunk of it before it reaches anywhere else (the first-pass effect). So doctors prescribe a bit extra to make sure enough drug survives! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T3#GNS125_U5_T3_h7)

question: A patient asks for a safe way to cook potatoes on a low-fat diet. What should you suggest?

options.A: Baked or boiled without butter or sour cream
options.B: Pan-fried in rich bacon drippings for flavor
options.C: Deep-fried in vegetable oil until golden brown
options.D: Smashed with heavy whipping cream and whole milk

explanation: Exactly! Potatoes are naturally fat-free, but you must skip the added butter, cream, or oils. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T006#GNS227_U6_T006_h3)

question: What makes a disaster different from a normal medical emergency?

options.A: An emergency never requires outside assistance.
options.B: A disaster affects only one patient at a time.
options.C: An emergency only happens inside a hospital building.
options.D: A disaster overwhelms local resources and community systems.

explanation: You've got this! A disaster is so big that it exhausts local clinics, hospitals, and supplies, meaning extra help from regional or national levels is needed. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T3#GNS315_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why do we need clear, agreed-upon definitions when collecting data for quality improvement?

options.A: To ensure everyone interprets and measures terms in the exact same way
options.B: To make the research paper long enough for publication
options.C: To increase the financial budget allocated to the nursing unit
options.D: To prove that nurses are working faster than doctors

explanation: Clear definitions mean everyone is speaking the same language, so the data we collect across different shifts is reliable and true. [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT an indication for manual vacuum aspiration?

options.A: Endometrial biopsy for abnormal uterine bleeding
options.B: Management of a full-term normal vaginal delivery
options.C: First-trimester elective termination of pregnancy
options.D: Incomplete miscarriage with retained tissue

explanation: MVA is restricted to first-trimester uterine evacuation and diagnostic sampling, not full-term deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of an internalizing intentional injury?

options.A: Physical assault
options.B: Gang fighting
options.C: Suicide attempt
options.D: Armed robbery

explanation: Correct! Self-harm and suicide attempts are directed inward against oneself, which makes them internalizing intentional injuries. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T7#GNS312_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why is it important to know a germ's 'portal of exit' when caring for an infectious patient?

options.A: It calculates the total number of pathogens living inside the host.
options.B: It helps predict how the pathogen might leave the body to spread to others.
options.C: It determines the specific blood type compatibility of the host.
options.D: It reveals the exact genetic mutation rate of the invading organism.

explanation: Spot-on! Understanding the portal of exit shows you how germs leave the body (like through coughs or body fluids) so you can put up barriers and stop them. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a school health programme?

options.A: To eliminate the need for community health workers
options.B: To penalize teachers whose classes have poor attendance records
options.C: To measure success, identify gaps, and improve service delivery
options.D: To calculate the exact financial profits of the school canteen

explanation: Correct! Checking in on the programme helps us see what is working well and fix areas that need more attention. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h8)

question: A patient is unconscious and unable to swallow safely. What is a main reason to insert an NG tube?

options.A: To permanently cure the underlying brain injury
options.B: To provide safe enteral nutrition and hydration
options.C: To prevent the patient from moving in bed
options.D: To replace the need for routine oral hygiene care

explanation: If a patient can't swallow safely, we still need to feed them! An NG tube lets us deliver food and water straight to the stomach without choking risks. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T1#GNS212_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is a direct consequence of severe undernutrition?

options.A: Rapid increase in bone mineral density
options.B: Muscle wasting and weak immune response
options.C: Lowered risk of developing pressure injuries
options.D: Enhanced ability to fight off surgical infections

explanation: When the body lacks enough nutrients, it breaks down its own muscle tissue for energy and fails to produce enough immune cells to fight infections. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h4)

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: To ensure that hospitals charge the correct fees for admissions
options.B: To punish clinics that fail to treat enough patients each month
options.C: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on healthy volunteer populations
options.D: To collect and analyze health data for early detection and planning

explanation: Exactly! Surveillance is like a early-warning radar. It tracks disease patterns continuously so health workers can spot trouble and plan ahead. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T76#GNS214_U1_T76_h3)

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance for infectious diseases?

options.A: Ongoing collection and analysis of health data to guide public health action
options.B: Enforcing strict legal penalties for healthcare facilities that break sterile technique
options.C: Manufacture of safe and effective vaccines for global distribution
options.D: Providing emergency medical treatment to individual hospital patients

explanation: Correct! Tracking disease numbers helps public health teams spot trends and stop outbreaks early. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h8)

question: What term is used when people delay or refuse vaccines even though they are available?

options.A: Herd immunity
options.B: Vaccine hesitancy
options.C: Cold chain failure
options.D: Antigen fatigue

explanation: Spot on! 'Vaccine hesitancy' describes when people feel unsure or hold back from getting vaccinated due to various doubts or worries. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h8)

question: What is the best approach when a nurse gives dietary advice to a patient with a chronic condition?

options.A: Telling the patient to rely entirely on vitamin supplements instead of food
options.B: Focusing solely on what foods the patient must completely ban from the house
options.C: Tailoring advice to fit the patient's cultural background, finances, and lifestyle
options.D: Handing out a strict, pre-printed meal plan that cannot be changed

explanation: Spot on! Advice only works if it fits into the patient's real life, budget, and cultural preferences. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T009#GNS227_U4_T009_h7)

question: What is a major reason why children end up roaming the streets in many communities?

options.A: Excessive participation in organized school sports
options.B: Severe poverty and financial hardship at home
options.C: Strict adherence to traditional cultural values
options.D: Overabundance of free government-provided housing

explanation: Spot on. Extreme financial hardship at home often forces families to send children out to find money, leaving them exposed and vulnerable on the streets. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which type of scale is best suited for an adult patient who is completely unable to stand?

options.A: A specialized chair or bed scale
options.B: A standard beam balance scale
options.C: A hanging infant spring scale
options.D: A flat digital floor scale

explanation: Chair and bed scales allow nurses to obtain accurate weights for immobile patients without forcing them to stand. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why can altering a ready-made topical cream cause problems?

options.A: It changes the expiration date to the exact same day
options.B: It breaks down the product stability and preservatives
options.C: It automatically turns the lotion into a liquid
options.D: It causes the active ingredient to evaporate instantly

explanation: Mixing products messes up the chemical balance and can make it easier for bacteria to grow. Don't worry, you'll get the hang of product safety in no time! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h1)

question: What happens if a patient starts eating a lot of fiber but forgets to drink enough water?

options.A: The patient will immediately develop severe watery diarrhea
options.B: Constipation can actually worsen because stool becomes dry and bulky
options.C: Kidney function will fail due to excess nutrient absorption
options.D: Fiber will pass through the body completely unchanged

explanation: Remember: fiber acts like a sponge! Without water, it cannot swell properly and will just form a hard, difficult lump in the gut. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why are sympathomimetic drugs often called 'fight-or-flight' medications?

options.A: They mimic the natural body response to stress and danger
options.B: They force the digestive system to process food rapidly
options.C: They completely shut down the central nervous system
options.D: They lower the heart rate to conserve body energy

explanation: Spot on! These drugs copy adrenaline, which naturally gears your body up to handle emergencies by opening airways and boosting energy. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T5#GNS223_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why can high levels of positive pressure ventilation sometimes cause a patient's blood pressure to drop?

options.A: It increases the heart rate so high that filling time is eliminated
options.B: It increases pressure inside the chest, which reduces blood return to the heart
options.C: It forces fluid directly out of the vascular system into the tissues
options.D: It directly causes systemic vasodilation through chemical release

explanation: Think of the chest as a closed box. Pumping too much air in crowds the major veins, making it harder for blood to flow back to the heart, which dips the blood pressure. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T6#GNS315_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why must blood pressure be lowered slowly during a hypertensive emergency?

options.A: Rapid drops can cause dangerous lack of blood flow to vital organs
options.B: Fast drops trigger permanent damage to peripheral nerve endings
options.C: Slow reductions prevent the kidneys from excreting excess potassium
options.D: Gradual changes allow oral medications time to absorb fully

explanation: Well done! Dropping pressure too fast when the body is used to high levels can starve the brain and heart of blood flow and cause a stroke or heart attack. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T2#GNS223_U1_T2_h7)

question: What does the 'Great Man' theory say about leadership?

options.A: Leadership qualities are inherited at birth
options.B: Anyone can learn to lead through weekend workshops
options.C: Only senior physicians are capable of guiding ward staff
options.D: Leadership depends entirely on the surrounding environment

explanation: The Great Man theory suggests that great leaders are born with natural talents, rather than trained. A bit old-school, but an important concept to know! [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h2)

question: A patient says they prefer taking their bath in the evening right before sleep, instead of the morning. What should you do?

options.A: Insist that morning baths are the only way to stop skin sores
options.B: Adjust the routine to accommodate the patient's personal preference
options.C: Tell them hospital rules say baths must happen before breakfast
options.D: Refuse because evening shifts are too busy

explanation: You're a star! Whenever it's clinically safe, always respect your patient's personal routine to make them feel at home in the hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h8)

question: As a midwife checking the lower boundary of the pelvic cavity, which bones help form the pelvic outlet?

options.A: Acetabulum and pubic tubercle
options.B: Ischial tuberosities and coccyx
options.C: Linea terminalis and sacral ala
options.D: Iliac crests and sacral promontory

explanation: Think of the bottom exit of the pelvis: it's bounded by your tailbone (coccyx), the sitting bones (ischial tuberosities), and the front pubic bone. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h4)

question: Which nutrient gives the body its fastest and main source of energy?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Minerals
options.C: Proteins
options.D: Vitamins

explanation: Carbs are our body's favorite quick energy snack! They break down fast into glucose to keep us going through lectures and ward rounds. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h2)

question: What is a big plus of using hydrogen peroxide gas plasma compared to older gas methods?

options.A: It works instantly without needing any special packaging
options.B: It can be performed easily using standard washbasins
options.C: It operates at low temperatures and leaves no toxic residue
options.D: It is the cheapest method available for hospital wards

explanation: Gas plasma is gentle on delicate equipment and breaks down into harmless water and oxygen, skipping the long wait for aeration. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to discover local food taboos in a new community?

options.A: Fining families who refuse to eat eggs and meat in public
options.B: Publishing a questionnaire in international medical journals
options.C: Reporting the village elders to the federal ministry of health
options.D: Conducting focus groups and talking with key community leaders

explanation: Community assessment is all about direct engagement! Friendly talks and respectful discussions with local stakeholders uncover these practices best. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h6)

question: Which of these situations clearly calls for an emergency medical evacuation?

options.A: A simple closed fracture in a cooperative adult
options.B: Uncontrolled internal hemorrhage needing surgery
options.C: Mild dehydration responding well to oral fluids
options.D: Stable chronic hypertension controlled by oral meds

explanation: When a patient has a life-threatening surgical emergency that your clinic can't handle, you need to transfer them quickly to a facility ready for operations. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why is evaluation considered an essential final step in the directing process?

options.A: It helps managers spot problems and adjust their approach for better care
options.B: It is required by law to punish nurses who make mistakes on duty
options.C: It proves to the hospital board that the manager is working hard
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any future shift planning

explanation: Continuous evaluation provides the feedback loop needed to refine leadership strategies and protect patient safety. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h8)

question: Which nursing diagnosis fits best when a patient struggles to use good defense mechanisms and falls back on unhealthy coping patterns?

options.A: Ineffective thermoregulation
options.B: Impaired physical mobility
options.C: Ineffective coping
options.D: Deficient fluid volume

explanation: When life stressors outweigh a person's current tools for handling them, 'Ineffective coping' is the exact NANDA diagnosis we reach for. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h6)

question: When a baker uses yeast to make dough rise, which gas makes it happen?

options.A: Ethanol alcohol
options.B: Lactic acid crystals
options.C: Citric acid drops
options.D: Carbon dioxide gas

explanation: Spot on! Yeast feeds on sugars and releases tiny bubbles of carbon dioxide gas, which gets trapped and makes the dough fluffy and rise. [learn more](GST114_U3_T5#GST114_U3_T5_h2)

question: A patient's wound dressing is soaked in pus and drainage. Which waste category does it go into?

options.A: Radioactive waste
options.B: General domestic waste
options.C: Infectious waste
options.D: Pharmaceutical waste

explanation: Any material heavily soiled with blood, pus, or body fluids can spread infection, so it must go straight into the infectious waste bin. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h3)

question: Why would a researcher choose to observe heavy drinkers instead of forcing an experiment where people drink alcohol for years?

options.A: Alcohol abuse is too rare to study in a clinical trial setting
options.B: Experimental trials cannot use statistical analysis
options.C: Observational studies are much more expensive to conduct
options.D: It is unethical to force participants to consume alcohol for an experiment

explanation: Well reasoned! We can never intentionally put people in harm's way or force them to take harmful substances just for an experiment. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h5)

question: A nurse manager wants an evaluation tool that matches scores with real-life workplace actions. Which tool works best?

options.A: Annual patient billing and insurance records
options.B: General peer gossip collected over lunch breaks
options.C: Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales (BARS)
options.D: A simple single-item attendance checklist

explanation: BARS is a fancy term for a very practical tool. It pairs numbers with clear descriptions of actual behavior so grading isn't just a guessing game. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h3)

question: After passing the corona radiata, which protective layer of the egg does the sperm bind to next?

options.A: Cervical os
options.B: Fimbriae
options.C: Zona pellucida
options.D: Endometrium

explanation: That's right! The zona pellucida is a clear, tough gel-like layer surrounding the egg with special parking spots (receptors) for sperm. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T8#GNS121_U5_T8_h4)

question: During which weeks of pregnancy is a baby most at risk for birth defects from harmful drugs?

options.A: The first two weeks following conception
options.B: The final two weeks before anticipated birth
options.C: Weeks three through eight of the first trimester
options.D: Throughout the entire third trimester

explanation: This is the major window when little organs are actively forming (organogenesis), making weeks 3 to 8 the most sensitive time. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h3)

question: When a mosquito bites you and passes on the malaria parasite, what kind of transmission is this?

options.A: Contact transmission
options.B: Vehicle-borne transmission
options.C: Vector-borne transmission
options.D: Droplet transmission

explanation: Vectors are living creatures, like mosquitoes or ticks, that carry germs from one person or animal to another. Great clinical connection for Nigerian nursing practice! [learn more](GST114_U3_T2#GST114_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why is it important to monitor pressure and volume during mechanical ventilation?

options.A: It controls the exact body temperature of the patient
options.B: It means you never have to listen to breath sounds with a stethoscope
options.C: It guarantees the patient will be off the machine by morning
options.D: It ensures the machine supports breathing safely without injuring the lungs

explanation: Tracking pressures helps prevent lung damage (barotrauma) while making sure the patient gets enough oxygen. Safety first! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T2#GNS315_U4_T2_h5)

question: When the Ebola virus enters the human body, which immune cells does it attack first?

options.A: Red blood cells and platelets
options.B: Epithelial cells of the skin
options.C: Macrophages and monocytes
options.D: Neuron cells in the brain

explanation: Spot on! The virus tricks our body by attacking our own defense cells (macrophages and monocytes) right from the start. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why shouldn't you crowd a pie chart with too many categories?

options.A: The total percentage will exceed 100 percent
options.B: Computer software cannot calculate angles for them
options.C: Statistical rules ban charts with more than four bars
options.D: The slices become too small and hard to read

explanation: Exactly! Too many slices turn your chart into a tiny, unreadable puzzle. Keep it simple and clear! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T8#GNS217_U4_T8_h3)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with severe belly pain and rectal bleeding after using a local herbal enema. What is the biggest nursing concern here?

options.A: Severe allergic rhinitis and upper airway swelling
options.B: Sudden complete obstruction of the upper esophagus
options.C: Trauma to the rectal mucosa and systemic toxicity
options.D: Immediate development of peripheral neuropathy

explanation: Harsh local enemas can easily tear the delicate lining of the rectum and quickly push strong, unmeasured chemicals straight into the bloodstream. Ouch! Patient safety is key here. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T2#GNS125_U2_T2_h5)

question: How does risk pooling benefit hospitals within the HMO framework?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever getting sick again
options.B: It guarantees a steady and predictable flow of income for operations
options.C: It allows them to charge any price they want for surgery
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nurses and doctors

explanation: By collecting regular fees from many enrollees, the HMO ensures hospitals receive consistent payments instead of depending on erratic cash from individual patients. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h2)

question: Why do milk-borne disease outbreaks often hit many people in a neighborhood all at once?

options.A: Many consumers drank from the same contaminated batch of milk
options.B: The illness spreads directly through person-to-person coughing
options.C: Public water systems carry the bacteria through house pipes
options.D: Local weather changes activate dormant spores in the air

explanation: Exactly! When a single contaminated batch of dairy is sent out to many local homes, it naturally causes a sudden cluster of sick people in the community. [learn more](GST114_U3_T4#GST114_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why is the cortical reaction important right when fertilization happens?

options.A: It prevents more than one sperm from entering the egg
options.B: It helps the fertilized egg travel down the fallopian tube
options.C: It provides extra energy for the newly formed zygote
options.D: It speeds up the process of genetic material fusion

explanation: Once the first lucky sperm gets inside, the egg quickly changes its outer coat to lock out all other sperm. It's like a VIP bouncer keeping things orderly! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h3)

question: When must a nurse researcher use non-parametric statistical tests?

options.A: When the research study is funded by a government hospital
options.B: When the data does not follow a normal bell curve distribution
options.C: When the sample size is extremely large and perfectly random
options.D: When all study variables are measured on a continuous scale

explanation: Brilliant! If your data is messy or skewed and doesn't fit that neat bell-shaped curve, non-parametric tests save the day. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which leadership style is most appropriate during a sudden cardiac arrest emergency?

options.A: Democratic
options.B: Laissez-faire
options.C: Delegative
options.D: Autocratic

explanation: An emergency requires fast, clear, direct instructions without debates, making autocratic leadership essential. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h5)

question: What is a major safety risk for patients with Pick's disease due to temporal lobe changes?

options.A: Developing sudden and severe bone fractures from walking
options.B: Inability to feel pain when touching hot stove surfaces
options.C: Sudden loss of hearing making them unable to hear fire alarms
options.D: Attempting to eat non-food objects or dangerous substances

explanation: Because of changes in how they experience things orally, these patients might try to chew or swallow harmful objects. Keeping hazardous items out of reach is a crucial nursing priority! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of disaster preparedness in nursing?

options.A: To entirely prevent natural disasters from occurring in local communities
options.B: To reduce the financial operational costs of running a public hospital
options.C: To ensure a rapid and effective clinical response when a crisis strikes
options.D: To punish staff who fail to report for emergency duty shifts

explanation: You've got this! Preparedness is all about taking smart steps before a crisis hits so our healthcare teams can jump in quickly and save lives when emergencies happen. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h1)

question: During early planning, why is open brainstorming without immediate criticism so helpful?

options.A: It encourages team members to share many creative ideas freely
options.B: It ensures that the first suggestion given is always the best one
options.C: It prevents nurses from talking about clinical errors openly
options.D: It speeds up the final approval process by hospital management

explanation: When people aren't afraid of being judged, they feel safe throwing out creative and fun solutions. No idea is a bad idea during brainstorming! [learn more](GST319_U3_T3#GST319_U3_T3_h3)

question: What term describes how consistent and repeatable a research measurement tool is?

options.A: Randomization
options.B: External validity
options.C: Selection bias
options.D: Reliability

explanation: If a tool is reliable, you can trust it to give you consistent results every single time you use it, no matter who is holding it. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h7)

question: A patient spends an hour doing a hand-washing ritual before meals. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Allow time for the ritual initially, then work with the patient to gradually set limits
options.B: Immediately shut off the water supply and force the patient to sit at the table
options.C: Administer a stat dose of intravenous antipsychotic medication to stop the habit
options.D: Scold the patient firmly to teach them that the behavior is completely useless

explanation: Spot on! Never cut them off cold turkey right away. Give them time at first, then gently help them reduce it over time. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T7#GNS314_U2_T7_h6)

question: What causes dizziness when a pregnant woman lies flat on her back?

options.A: An acute drop in blood glucose levels caused by the fetus
options.B: Reduced venous return caused by uterine compression of the vena cava
options.C: Sudden dehydration from excessive sweating during sleep
options.D: Spasms of the cerebral arteries due to high progesterone

explanation: Spot on! The heavy womb presses on the big vein (vena cava), slowing blood return to the heart and making her feel dizzy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T2#GNS121_U7_T2_h5)

question: What is a major drawback of rapid bolus tube feedings?

options.A: They must run continuously for the entire day
options.B: They require expensive electronic pump machinery
options.C: They can cause nausea, cramping, and fullness
options.D: They completely eliminate normal bowel sounds

explanation: Pouring a large volume of formula into the stomach too fast overwhelms the organ, frequently leading to abdominal discomfort and vomiting. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h4)

question: What can happen if educators overlook cultural differences in communication?

options.A: They will automatically improve student test scores in pharmacology
options.B: They remove all language barriers from clinical wards
options.C: They ensure all students learn at the exact same speed
options.D: They might misinterpret a student's respectful quietness as laziness

explanation: In some cultures, staying completely quiet around elders or teachers is a sign of deep respect. Instructors need to understand this so they don't misjudge a student. [learn more](GST321_U8_T9#GST321_U8_T9_h5)

question: How does your job as a nurse change when you step out of a normal hospital and into a disaster zone?

options.A: The nurse only focuses on administrative paperwork
options.B: The nurse must rely more on quick improvisations and resource-scarce settings
options.C: The nurse works exclusively with advanced robotic surgical tools
options.D: The nurse stops providing direct patient care entirely

explanation: Disasters mess up normal hospital supplies, so you'll often have to think on your feet and make the best of what's available around you. It's tough, but Nigerian nurses do it brilliantly! [learn more](GNS315_U5_T5#GNS315_U5_T5_h1)

question: In drug supply and logistics, what does the term CIF stand for?

options.A: Cost, Insurance, and Freight
options.B: Client Invoice and Fee
options.C: Capital, Inventory, and Finance
options.D: Central Immunization Fund

explanation: CIF is just a handy shipping term! It covers the actual purchase price of imported drugs plus the cost of insurance and getting them safely delivered. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T5#GNS215_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which cranial nerve carries hearing and balance messages from the ear to the brain?

options.A: Cranial nerve VIII
options.B: Cranial nerve V
options.C: Cranial nerve II
options.D: Cranial nerve X

explanation: Cranial nerve VIII is also known as the vestibulocochlear nerve—combining balance (vestibule) and hearing (cochlea) into one pathway! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T2#GNS211_U4_T2_h7)

question: What special proteins does the body make to neutralize foreign invaders or antigens?

options.A: Enzymes
options.B: Antibodies
options.C: Platelets
options.D: Hormones

explanation: Spot on! Antibodies are the body's custom-built defense proteins that lock onto and disarm specific foreign invaders. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T11#GNS313_U2_T11_h2)

question: What does a high dropout rate mean in an immunization program?

options.A: Every child in the community is fully immunized
options.B: The health facility has a surplus of vaccine stock
options.C: Children started vaccination but failed to finish
options.D: The community rejects all forms of modern medicine

explanation: A dropout rate simply tracks the kids who took their first dose (like Pentavalent 1) but didn't return to complete the full series. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T75#GNS214_U1_T75_h2)

question: Why are intangible costs hard to track in a standard budget?

options.A: They cannot be easily measured with a monetary price
options.B: They only happen after the patient leaves the hospital
options.C: They are fully covered by standard health insurance policies
options.D: They are completely preventable with proper hand hygiene

explanation: You cannot easily put a price tag on human pain and emotional stress, so hospital budgets struggle to measure them. [learn more](GST322_U2_T1#GST322_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is considered an Activity of Daily Living (ADL)?

options.A: Driving a car to work
options.B: Bathing and dressing
options.C: Cooking complex meals
options.D: Balancing a bank account

explanation: ADLs are basic self-care tasks required for daily living, including bathing, dressing, eating, and toileting. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h3)

question: What are the coarse hairs located inside the nasal vestibule called?

options.A: Vibrissae
options.B: Turbinates
options.C: Cilia
options.D: Microvilli

explanation: Vibrissae are the stiff, coarse hairs at the entrance of the nose that catch large bugs, dust, and debris. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h5)

question: What major problem does the Incident Command System prevent when multiple agencies respond to a disaster?

options.A: Shortages of basic food items in grocery stores
options.B: Patients refusing to take their prescribed emergency medications
options.C: Confusion over authority and duplicated efforts among responding groups
options.D: The physical destruction of hospital buildings by storms

explanation: Exactly! Without ICS, different teams might bump heads or waste time doing the exact same job. It keeps everyone organized! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of emotional distress in a patient?

options.A: Sudden and severe social withdrawal
options.B: Persistent sadness and frequent crying
options.C: Expressing feelings of total hopelessness
options.D: Steady weight gain and cheerful laughter

explanation: Laughter and a steady weight are generally positive signs! Crying, hopelessness, and pulling away from people are the red flags we look out for. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h6)

question: What does continuous professional development help maintain in a nursing team?

options.A: Fewer working hours for night shifts
options.B: A lower overall patient bed capacity
options.C: Strict separation between doctors and nurses
options.D: Up-to-date clinical knowledge and best practices

explanation: Spot on! Keeping our skills fresh through continuous learning ensures we give our patients the very best, modern care possible. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why do nurses always do a double-check before giving high-risk medications?

options.A: To eliminate the need for patient wristband scanning
options.B: To catch calculation or transcription errors before administration
options.C: To reduce the time spent documenting on the computer
options.D: To comply with insurance billing requirements for intensive care

explanation: Having a second pair of eyes helps catch little math or dosage mistakes that anyone could miss when tired. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T7#GNS113_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why is careful preparation a must before transferring an unstable disaster patient to another hospital?

options.A: It allows the nurse to take a long break during transport.
options.B: It ensures the receiving hospital never has to buy medical supplies.
options.C: Moving patients without stabilization and monitoring can lead to rapid clinical deterioration.
options.D: Transfer paperwork is the only legal requirement in disaster zones.

explanation: Correct! Bumping along in a vehicle can dislodge lines or worsen shock if the patient isn't properly stabilized and monitored before the journey begins. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h6)

question: A family member wants to help their sibling remember daily HIV medications. What is a great first step?

options.A: Take the medication alongside the patient every single time
options.B: Wait until the patient misses three doses before speaking
options.C: Hide the medications in the kitchen to maintain privacy
options.D: Set daily phone alarms together to signal pill times

explanation: Smart thinking! Setting reliable phone alarms together is a practical way to build a steady daily routine for taking meds on time. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h3)

question: What severe medical condition is directly caused by prolonged, blocked labor in young girls whose pelvises are not yet fully grown?

options.A: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.B: Obstetric fistula
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Pregnancy-induced hypertension

explanation: Well done! The baby's head presses too long against an immature pelvis, creating a hole between the birth canal and bladder or rectum. This leads to constant leakage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T11#GNS312_U1_T11_h3)

question: What can happen if the pelvic ligaments and fascia become weak?

options.A: Blood flow to the lower limbs is cut off
options.B: The thigh bones become unstable in the socket
options.C: Pelvic organs can descend or prolapse
options.D: Abdominal muscles stop contracting properly

explanation: Spot on. Without strong support from ligaments and fascia, gravity pulls the pelvic organs downward. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of emergency classification in nursing?

options.A: Determining which nurse works which shift
options.B: Sorting patients based on medical urgency
options.C: Reducing the total number of hospital admissions
options.D: Calculating the final hospital bill for the patient

explanation: Emergency classification helps nurses quickly organize patients by how sick they are so the most critical ones get treated first. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h1)

question: A community nurse is mapping health risks in a rural village. What is the best way to find pregnant teenage brides?

options.A: Reviewing national census reports published every ten years
options.B: Partnering with local women leaders and tracking school dropout patterns
options.C: Waiting in urban tertiary hospitals for emergency referrals to arrive
options.D: Relying solely on self-reporting via digital mobile phone surveys

explanation: Local women leaders and school attendance logs give nurses the best grassroots view of which young girls are dropping out and entering marriages. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is a normal finding and NOT a reason to refer a client to a special clinic?

options.A: Routine spontaneous passage of small lochial blood clots
options.B: Underlying chronic illness requiring careful risk assessment
options.C: History of severe adverse side effects with previous pills
options.D: Desire for long-acting reversible contraception like an implant

explanation: Passing small blood clots early in the postpartum period is totally normal and expected, so it does not need a special referral. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h4)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility regarding medication management in adult day care?

options.A: Prescribing new medications whenever a client reports mild discomfort
options.B: Manufacturing custom pharmaceutical compounds on-site for each client
options.C: Allowing clients to share their prescription drugs freely among peers
options.D: Verifying orders, administering or supervising intake, and monitoring for side effects

explanation: Nurses ensure medication safety by checking dosages, administering or supervising consumption, and watching closely for adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h6)

question: What common problem can happen if a patient wears a poorly fitted prosthetic limb?

options.A: Skin breakdown and pressure ulcers
options.B: Complete recovery of muscle strength
options.C: Rapid elevation of blood pressure
options.D: Sudden permanent loss of vision

explanation: Friction from ill-fitting gear is tough on fragile skin and can quickly lead to painful sores. Good nursing assessment catches this early! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T15#GNS225_U5_T15_h5)

question: What is the main goal of taking and handing over on the ward?

options.A: To transfer patient care responsibilities safely between shifts
options.B: To replace formal written patient medical records completely
options.C: To give nurses a chance to socialise before starting work
options.D: To allow doctors to check if nurses are doing their jobs

explanation: Handover makes sure that important care details move securely from the outgoing nurse to the incoming one, so no patient is left unprotected! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h1)

question: If a young patient has early cervical changes but wants to have children in the future, which procedure removes the abnormal tissue while protecting her fertility?

options.A: Cervical conization
options.B: Pelvic exenteration
options.C: Total abdominal hysterectomy
options.D: Oophorectomy

explanation: You nailed it! Conization takes out a cone-shaped wedge of the cervix containing the abnormal cells. Because the rest of the uterus is left alone, future pregnancies are still possible. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h7)

question: During which part of pregnancy do a mother's daily food energy (calorie) needs go up the most?

options.A: Third trimester
options.B: The first two weeks postpartum
options.C: During active labor
options.D: First trimester

explanation: As the baby gets bigger towards the end of pregnancy, calorie needs peak—demanding extra energy to cross the finish line! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h2)

question: A patient on combined pills reports mild nausea and tender breasts during her first week. What should you tell her?

options.A: Recommend immediate emergency surgery to check for blood clots
options.B: Reassure her that these are common mild adjustment side effects
options.C: Tell her to double her daily dose to help her body adjust faster
options.D: Instruct her to stop taking all medication immediately and report to the doctor

explanation: Take a breath—minor side effects are totally normal when starting estrogen as the body gets used to the new hormone levels. They usually clear up after a cycle or two! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h6)

question: How do local disaster teams handle poor or flooded roads during an emergency?

options.A: By waiting months until the floodwaters dry up completely
options.B: By demanding that heavy trucks drive through flooded bridges anyway
options.C: by halting all relief distribution until federal contractors fix the roads
options.D: By utilizing alternative transport methods like local boats, canoes, and motorcycles

explanation: Well done! When big trucks can't pass, using local boats, canoes, or bikes is a smart way to get supplies to people who are cut off. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which nursing action is an absolute must for a patient on a continuous paralytic drip in the ICU?

options.A: Applying lubricating eye drops and taping the eyelids shut
options.B: Encouraging the patient to perform deep breathing exercises hourly
options.C: Removing physical restraints so the patient can stretch their legs
options.D: Keeping the room completely dark so the patient can sleep deeply

explanation: Paralyzed patients can't blink, so their eyes dry out fast! Regular eye care prevents painful corneal scratches. You're thinking like a real nurse already! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the main reason iron supplements are routinely given to pregnant women?

options.A: To harden the fetal tooth enamel before delivery occurs
options.B: To prevent anemia caused by expanding blood volume and fetal demands
options.C: To lower maternal blood pressure during the third trimester
options.D: To speed up the digestion of complex proteins in the stomach

explanation: Because a pregnant mum's blood volume shoots up, her body needs extra iron to build all those extra red blood cells without running low. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T49#GNS214_U1_T49_h4)

question: What is the primary factor that food pricing reflects in a basic economic sense?

options.A: The arbitrary decisions made by local retail store owners
options.B: The total amount of money printed by the federal government
options.C: The cost to produce, transport, and sell food balanced with consumer demand
options.D: The fixed value assigned to crops by international health organizations

explanation: Food prices are fundamentally tied to the expenses involved in bringing food from the farm to the table, weighed against what buyers can pay. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h1)

question: Why should a nurse remind patients using mydriatic (pupil-dilating) drops to wear sunglasses outside?

options.A: The medication changes the natural color of the iris
options.B: Bright sunlight can make the cornea swell up rapidly
options.C: Ultraviolet rays will destroy the active drug
options.D: Their widened pupils let in way too much glaring light

explanation: When pupils are forced wide open by drops, they can't shrink down to block bright sunlight. Sunglasses save the patient from painful glare! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary function of an antibody in the human body?

options.A: To produce energy for cellular reactions
options.B: To carry oxygen to body tissues
options.C: To identify and neutralize foreign antigens
options.D: To clot blood after an injury occurs

explanation: Antibodies are immune proteins designed to bind specifically to foreign invaders and toxins, marking them for destruction. [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h1)

question: A cargo ship is 50 miles from port when a crew member gets a non-emergency infection. What is the best first step?

options.A: Place the patient in a life raft and tow them toward land.
options.B: Consult shoreside medical advice and evaluate if a port diversion or coastal rendezvous is needed.
options.C: Wait until the cargo ship completes its entire transatlantic voyage.
options.D: Demand an immediate emergency helicopter hoist regardless of the weather.

explanation: Well done! Since it's not an instant life-or-death emergency, you can plan a safe option like steering toward a nearby port instead of risking a dangerous helicopter lift. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h6)

question: How does assertive behavior differ from aggressive behavior?

options.A: Assertiveness requires shouting to be heard clearly
options.B: Aggression is used exclusively by senior nursing staff
options.C: Assertiveness attacks the issue rather than the person
options.D: Aggression always leads to better patient outcomes

explanation: While aggression targets and belittles individuals, assertiveness keeps the focus firmly on solving the professional problem. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h1)

question: Your heart beats and your food digests automatically without you having to think about it. Which system runs this show?

options.A: Cerebellar motor system
options.B: Central reflex system
options.C: Somatic nervous system
options.D: Autonomic nervous system

explanation: The autonomic system runs automatically in the background so you can focus on your nursing notes. Well done! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary role of progesterone during the majority of a normal pregnancy?

options.A: To maintain uterine muscle relaxation and prevent early contractions
options.B: To trigger the posterior pituitary gland to release large amounts of oxytocin
options.C: To actively stimulate the frequent ripening of the uterine cervix
options.D: To raise maternal blood glucose levels for the growing fetus

explanation: Progesterone acts as a relaxant on the smooth muscle of the uterus, keeping it quiet and preventing premature labour throughout gestation. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h4)

question: Why do economists look at health spending as a percentage of GNP rather than just raw cash amounts?

options.A: It stops inflation from happening in local community pharmacies
options.B: It calculates the exact salary every registered nurse should earn
options.C: It allows fair comparison between countries with different economic sizes and populations
options.D: It predicts the exact number of disease outbreaks in a year

explanation: Using percentages helps us fairly compare health spending between big economies and smaller nations without getting confused by different currency values. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is a core pillar of the National Drug Policy?

options.A: Mandatory retirement age for pharmacists
options.B: Quality, safety, and efficacy of medicines
options.C: Privatization of all public teaching hospitals
options.D: Elimination of nursing schools in rural areas

explanation: Spot on! Making sure drugs are safe, work properly (efficacy), and are top quality is the heart of any good drug policy. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h3)

question: In many Nigerian homes, who is often involved when making healthcare decisions for an elderly patient?

options.A: Only the youngest child living in the household
options.B: Extended family networks and community elders
options.C: Foreign medical tourism agencies exclusively
options.D: The neighborhood security guards on duty

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare decisions in our local settings are often communal, bringing in extended family members and respected elders to support the patient. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T4#GNS324_U2_T4_h4)

question: What do we call a live, real-time tele-nursing session?

options.A: Mailing written symptom diaries to the clinic
options.B: Automated tracking of vital signs overnight
options.C: Sending recorded messages for later review
options.D: Real-time interaction using live video or phone calls

explanation: Synchronous care is just like a live phone or video chat where you and the patient talk and respond to each other right away! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which of these commonly causes frustration when using mobile nursing technology on the ward?

options.A: Too many physical stairs in modern multi-story hospitals
options.B: Dead batteries and poor wireless internet connectivity
options.C: Patients demanding to program the IV pumps themselves
options.D: Doctors refusing to let nurses touch computer carts

explanation: So true! Nothing slows down a shift quite like a dying battery or a spinning loading wheel when you're trying to chart quickly. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h6)

question: What should a caregiver do first if a child swallows a toxic household cleaner?

options.A: Force the child to drink large amounts of milk
options.B: Wait to see if the child develops a cough
options.C: Call emergency services or poison control immediately
options.D: Make the child vomit right away to clear the stomach

explanation: Certain chemicals can cause more damage if the person vomits, so professional guidance is required before taking action. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h5)

question: What is a Type A adverse drug reaction like?

options.A: It is bizarre and unrelated to the drug's normal actions
options.B: It is an allergic response mediated by the immune system
options.C: It is dose-dependent and predictable based on pharmacology
options.D: It only occurs when a patient stops taking a medication

explanation: Spot on! Type A reactions happen because the drug's normal effect is just too strong, usually when the dose is a bit too high for the patient. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h4)

question: How does the poliovirus mainly spread from person to person?

options.A: Vector-borne mosquito bites
options.B: Fecal-oral route
options.C: Direct sexual contact
options.D: Aerosol droplet inhalation

explanation: You've got this! The virus usually spreads when someone unknowingly eats or drinks something contaminated with tiny amounts of infected waste matter. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h1)

question: What is the main danger associated with postpartum hemorrhage in new mothers?

options.A: Permanent loss of the ability to walk
options.B: Severe allergic reactions to routine food
options.C: Chronic high blood pressure lasting years
options.D: Sudden and severe blood loss leading to shock

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage involves heavy bleeding after birth, which can quickly drop blood pressure and cause life-threatening shock if untreated. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h2)

question: Which of these is a strict 'no-go' (absolute contraindication) for putting in an IUD?

options.A: Mild iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Having had a past cesarean section
options.C: A history of high blood pressure
options.D: Confirmed or suspected pregnancy

explanation: Never place an IUD if a woman is already pregnant! It can cause serious complications, severe infection, or miscarriage. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to manage community medical waste?

options.A: Ensuring sharps containers are sealed before final disposal
options.B: Using puncture-resistant safety boxes for all used needles
options.C: Incinerating medical waste under controlled high temperatures
options.D: Throwing used syringes into ordinary household plastic garbage bags

explanation: Household bags easily puncture, exposing trash collectors and the public to contaminated needles. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is a huge risk factor for depression in older adults?

options.A: Having too many visiting family members
options.B: Social isolation and loneliness
options.C: Participating in regular group exercise classes
options.D: Living in a community with active social clubs

explanation: Being cut off from people takes a heavy toll on mental and physical health. Connection is medicine! [learn more](GNS321_U3_T3#GNS321_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is keeping a good stock of uterotonic drugs critical in a PAC unit?

options.A: To prevent or treat severe uterine bleeding and hemorrhage
options.B: To reverse the side effects of general anesthesia
options.C: To speed up the return of normal ovulation cycles
options.D: To relieve severe lower abdominal cramping pain

explanation: Uterotonics like oxytocin or misoprostol make the uterine muscle contract, which is a lifesaver for stopping dangerous blood loss after evacuation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h3)

question: Why does losing a massive amount of blood lead straight into shock?

options.A: The kidneys stop producing urine to save salt and water
options.B: Red blood cells multiply too fast and block small blood vessels
options.C: The heart beats too slowly to pump blood to the lungs
options.D: There is not enough fluid volume to maintain perfusion pressure

explanation: Without enough fluid in the pipes, the blood pressure drops, and vital organs don't get the blood flow they need. You're mastering the core concepts! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T3#GNS315_U2_T3_h4)

question: A patient shares that her husband constantly insults her, threatens to chase her out, and cuts her off from her family. What kind of abuse is this?

options.A: Traditional coercion
options.B: Psychological abuse
options.C: Physical maltreatment
options.D: Economic violence

explanation: Well done! Constant insults, threats, and isolation are designed to crush a person's self-esteem and mental peace. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h2)

question: How is Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) different from basic health education?

options.A: Basic health education focuses exclusively on preventing infectious diseases
options.B: BCC is only used inside hospital wards by qualified physicians and nurse specialists
options.C: BCC uses interactive dialogue and addresses social obstacles rather than just giving facts
options.D: Basic health education relies heavily on mass media television broadcasts

explanation: You've got it! While basic education just tells people what to do, BCC actually talks *with* them to figure out what's stopping them from living healthier lives. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T15#GNS313_U3_T15_h2)

question: How do instructional materials primarily help bridge the gap in nursing training?

options.A: By reducing the number of clinical hours required
options.B: By connecting abstract theory to practical clinical reality
options.C: By replacing hospital wards with computer simulations
options.D: By shortening the overall duration of nursing school

explanation: Visuals, models, and practical tools help students visualize difficult concepts they read in books before seeing them on real patients. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h1)

question: What common belief often drives high injection rates among patients in many local communities?

options.A: The recommendation of international health organizations
options.B: The lower financial cost of receiving intravenous drugs
options.C: The absence of any side effects from injectable drugs
options.D: The belief that injections work faster than oral medications

explanation: Many people strongly prefer injections because of the common myth that drugs given by needle cure illnesses much faster than pills. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h5)

question: If many experienced nurses travel abroad for better pay due to a recession, what is the immediate effect on the nurses left behind?

options.A: Complete elimination of night shift duties
options.B: Increased workloads and higher risk of burnout
options.C: Automatic promotion to senior administrative roles with less stress
options.D: Immediate doubling of the national healthcare budget

explanation: The 'japa' wave is real! When colleagues leave, remaining nurses face heavier patient loads and exhaustion. Taking care of your mental health is so important. [learn more](GST322_U3_T6#GST322_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why might a woman with Type III FGM need a procedure called defibulation during childbirth?

options.A: To prevent severe postpartum hemorrhage from the uterus
options.B: To allow the baby to pass through the narrowed vaginal opening
